author: Argoudpuy
body:
* **PTHR ID & PTN node:PTHR45990

* **Sequence to annotate (ID + gene/protein name):Q9UBZ9, REV1, DNA repair protein REV1

* ** According to PubMed=23143872, REV1 functions as a molecular adpator in the translesion synthesis (GO:0019985) and there is no evidence that this process (GO:0019985) is linked to deoxycytidyl transferase activity (GO:0017125).

* Add the label 'high priority' if needed. Generally high priority issues affect a lot of proteins, and annotations are incorrect (as opposed to just imprecise).
title: additional PAINT mapping for the adaptor activity  of REV1

author: ValWood
body:
This does look like a structural molecule (BRCT domain) 
In this case, can the older papers be flagged as "do not annotate" for this activity in Protein2GO? 

there does appear to be evidence  from human and yeast

human
https://academic.oup.com/nar/article/27/22/4468/1153151?login=false

yeast
https://www.yeastgenome.org/reference/S000051294

but presumably this activity is in another subunit?

@Argoudpuy  do we know which subunit, if any has this activity?

author: ValWood
Argoudpuy
body:
Hi Val,
it is a new activity in addition to its DNA template-dependent dCMP transferase activity. 
REV1 is a bifonctional protein. Functions as a molecular adpator in the translesion DNA synthesis independently of is DNA template-dependent dCMP transferase activity. In addition functions, the DNA template-dependent dCMP transferase activity for REV+ human has been shown only in vitro, but probably that plays a role during diversification of antibodies during somatic hypermutation (PubMed=16263170).
I hope tha helps
Guilaine

author: ValWood
body:
Right I understand. I thought you were suggesting that Rev1 didn't have deoxycytidyl transferase activity, and to remove the mapping.
I now understand that you want an additional PAINT mapping for the adaptor activity.
